questions.question: Self Introduction (Project-Oriented)
questions.answer: I have around 4.5 years of experience as a Java Full Stack Developer. Currently working on a customer onboarding and transaction processing system. Responsibilities include: Developing REST & Reactive APIs using Spring Boot & WebFlux, Handling high-volume traffic using non-blocking architecture, Integrating Kafka for async communication, Writing unit tests using JUnit & Mockito, and Frontend development using ReactJS. Achievements: Improved API performance using reactive programming, Implemented JWT-based authentication, Optimized microservices communication.

questions.question: What is Reactive Programming? Explain Mono vs Flux.
questions.answer: Reactive Programming is an asynchronous, non-blocking approach. Mono represents 0 or 1 element. Flux represents 0 to N elements. Used for handling high-concurrency applications with better resource utilization.

questions.question: Where do we use Mono?
questions.answer: Used when we expect a single result. Examples: Get user by ID, Login response, Payment status, Fetching bank account balance.

questions.question: How to call APIs using WebClient?
questions.answer: WebClient is Spring WebFlux's non-blocking HTTP client. Used to call external APIs asynchronously without blocking threads.

questions.question: How do you secure APIs?
questions.answer: Using Spring Security, JWT Authentication, Role-based authorization, HTTPS, Input validation, and CORS configuration.

questions.question: Explain JWT Authentication Workflow.
questions.answer: 1) User sends login credentials, 2) Server validates credentials, 3) JWT token generated, 4) Token sent to client, 5) Client sends token in header, 6) Server validates token using JWT Filter.

questions.question: What are HTTP Status Codes?
questions.answer: 200 OK, 201 Created, 400 Bad Request, 401 Unauthorized, 403 Forbidden, 404 Not Found, 500 Internal Server Error.

questions.question: Difference between 501 and 502?
questions.answer: 501 Not Implemented - Server doesn't support functionality. 502 Bad Gateway - Invalid response from upstream server.

questions.question: What is CORS?
questions.answer: CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing) allows cross-origin requests. Origin = protocol + host + port.

questions.question: What are Java 17 Features?
questions.answer: Records, Sealed Classes, Pattern Matching, Text Blocks, Enhanced Switch, Better Garbage Collectors, Improved Security.

questions.question: Explain Java 8 Supplier and Consumer.
questions.answer: Supplier provides values, Consumer consumes values.

questions.question: What is Method Reference?
questions.answer: Short form of lambda expression. Used for better readability and cleaner code.

questions.question: Explain CompletableFuture with example.
questions.answer: CompletableFuture is Java 8 feature for asynchronous programming. Supports chaining, combining multiple async computations, and exception handling.

questions.question: What is Executor Framework?
questions.answer: Used for background jobs, async processing, email sending, and thread pool management.

questions.question: Explain Callable and Future.
questions.answer: Callable returns a value. Future holds the result of asynchronous computation.

questions.question: Difference between parallelStream and flatMap?
questions.answer: parallelStream enables multi-threading. flatMap flattens nested collections.

questions.question: How to flatten List of List of List using streams?
questions.answer: Using multiple flatMap operations.

questions.question: Explain flatMap with example.
questions.answer: flatMap transforms each element into a stream and flattens.

questions.question: Difference between HashSet and TreeSet?
questions.answer: HashSet: O(1) operations, unordered. TreeSet: O(log n) operations, sorted.

questions.question: What is Composition vs Aggregation?
questions.answer: Composition - strong relationship (Car-Engine). Aggregation - weak relationship (School-Student).

questions.question: What are your strengths and weaknesses?
questions.answer: Strengths: Problem solving, Quick learner. Weakness: Sometimes focus too much on perfection.

questions.question: Why are you looking for a job change?
questions.answer: Looking for better growth, learning opportunities, and challenging work.

questions.question: Explain Builder vs Strategy Pattern.
questions.answer: Builder Pattern: Creates complex objects step by step. Strategy Pattern: Defines family of algorithms, encapsulates each one, and makes them interchangeable.
